candidates.text:
I literally can't think of a better risk/reward bet right now than building a ChatGPT plugin and getting in front of their 1.2 billion weekly users.

As of yesterday, ChatGPT recommends plugins in the middle of conversations. Millions of questions get asked every day with no plugin to recommend. Each one is an empty slot.

Facebook apps in 2007. iPhone apps in 2008. TikTok in 2019. Every big platform has a few months where distribution is free, and most people miss it.

I saw this firsthand when I lived in SF building venture backed companies. They are sacred times!

If I were starting this week:

1. Find a tool or workflow people already Google for or do by hand every week (PDF to Excel, invoice generator, weekly client reports)
2. Build it as a ChatGPT plugin
3. Write the description using the exact phrases people type into ChatGPT
4. Ship 5 of them and see which ones get picked up
5. Double down on the one with the most traction

In 12 months these slots will be crowded but right now they're pretty empty.

Most people will realize ChatGPT plugins were the biggest free distribution channel of 2026 sometime in 2027.

candidates.text:
since openai’s roadmap is pretty much entirely driven by x at this point (see ben thompson’s latest excellent piece), here’s what i would’ve done:

i probably would not have created a super app, instead i would’ve created two distinct product surfaces.

yes, i understand the downsides, esp heading toward an ipo, the need to grow codex users etc to prevent anthropic from running away with businesses + compute constraints. but almost every great tech company eventually became a collection of products either through acquisition or by building them. google has like 8 products with 2b+ users. fb has lots too.

the main problem is that trying to turn chatgpt into a super app has created an enormous amount of complexity (which i have written about). not just technically but cognitively. there are so many modes, tools, agents, surfaces, etc that even describing the product to a normal person is getting difficult. like how do you explain dots (which is yet another surface)?

chatgpt = insanely familiar consumer brand

codex = work + enterprise that everyone who mattered knew about

chatgpt agents could’ve become the perfect personal agents with simple, proactive, consumer first daily life things. imagine a daily feed, or proactive stuff that just works instead of having to schedule tasks.

codex agents could’ve become the enterprise agent surface that at deeply integrated into work, tools, browsers, terminals, company context, etc. imagine opening up the codex app & it’s simply ready for getting shit done. 

each surface could still have whatever primitives it needed like voice, browser, tools, connectors. the difference is that each product would have one extremely clear job. imagine at dev day you could say 1b active users on chat & 15m codex/business customers in one slide.

then launching new products becomes much easier. you can build highly opinionated interfaces for specific groups of users instead of continuously adding another abstraction into one increasingly complicated app.

& you could still share ~90% of the underlying infrastructure/code. the complexity gets pushed into product boundaries rather than onto the user.

i still really hate that it defaults to work when i want to chat & chat when i want to work.

anyway, just my two cents from completely outside the building.

candidates.text:
How Mark Zuckerberg wins AI: 

“AI is not, in fact, God. Instead, it does math and solves a limited set of problems humans face, and is otherwise simply useful and cool. Anthropic, and to a lesser extent OpenAI, have trouble ever accepting this fact. 

Zuckerberg does not. 

He has not spent a decade comparing his company to the Manhattan Project, and thus he is not above pushing the frontier of AI to help people book airline tickets, make dinner reservations, and edit photos. 

He will use it to drive down the cost of serving his users to zero, and to drive up his revenue by improving ads. He will use cash from the ad business—and his ownership of data centers, chips, and other infrastructure that Anthropic and OpenAI have to pay to rent—to undercut them on price. The potential install base for his AI is 3.6 billion people, who don’t care whether a given model is six months behind the frontier.

If AI commoditizes, then Anthropic and OpenAI go to zero, and value accrues instead at the complements Meta already dominates, like distribution, attention, personalization, and commerce. 

If it doesn’t commoditize, then at least he is not his competitors’ prisoner the way he’s been with Apple, and all he has to do is remain within six months of the frontier, which he’s already close to. Heads, he wins; tails, he wins.”

candidates.text:
Internal AI Usage Cap Memo:

In response to requests for increased AI budgets, they aren’t coming. And here’s why:

We currently offer 16x token spend per employee compared to the average of tech forward companies (Based on Ramp's spend data from 70,000 businesses). I say this to establish - for those of you who request increases, it is unlikely you will get it. Unlimited budgets create unlimited waste - a luxury we do not have. So, budget and use your tokens only on projects that have a clear revenue producing or cost savings. Otherwise, it's likely to be filed under "shit that doesn't matter and not worth spending money on."

To help you, we will be offering training(s) on:

How to figure out what's worth working on (biggest miss #1)
How to use fewer tokens to get same output (think of this like AI hygiene)
How to use the time AI saves you to be more effective

AI is a tool that creates leverage. It helps you get out more from what you put in. That said, company revenue is flat (relative terms) compared to AI usage increases. This suggests that people are (largely) using it on projects that don't matter, or are using it on things that do matter, then spending the saved time working on things that don't matter.

This discrepancy (difference between money we spend and money we make from AI) hints at a skill deficiency in the team. One which I hope we will train up - just as well as we trained up on AI usage.

So now that everyone is using it - it's time to use it well.

Let's crush Q4.

Alex

PS - The more clearly you can articulate how what you do generates a return, the more likely tokens will be in your future. And the way to maximize a return is to show HOW LITTLE you can use and HOW MUCH you can get from it.

What if we get paid 100% of salary in Bitcoin?
It could look a bit like this:

- 100% of my salary buys BTC
- It gets insta’ deposited into a yield position <1.2% APY
- is used in full as collateral
- Borrow USDC (or local stablecoin) to pay for monthly expenses. 
- next month more BTC enters the collateral and I borrow more local currency
- never sell BTC

What is the scenario where this could work?

- Deposit yield + BTC appreciation is higher than Borrowing interest
- fixed borrow APY
- No liquidity on trigger or having savings to start with to manage high LTV
- certainty that local currency will depreciate faster than BTC

Are any of these possible today?
